You are the cold reviewer in the principle-set-authoring process, its one screen (fresh context), run as the small-change process's check on req-2026-09-05-maker-self-check. Read only the two files named here — nothing else.

- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md
- artifact: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/principles.md (version 8 — the amendment is the fourth statement under define-good-up-front: "The maker of an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check, and record that it did." Judge the whole set against every scenario, but say for each finding whether it is in the amended statement or elsewhere.)

Prompt: "State, as judge_stamp, the model and prompt version you judge as. Read the criteria set at criteria_path and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact against every scenario. Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name, the quoted text, the change, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes."

Return exactly this structure:
judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v6
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, or "uncovered">
  section: <principle / statement>
  in_amendment: yes | no
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the criteria. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file.

13	# Founding principles
14	
15	## What a good principle looks like
16	
17	A principle is a standing rule about how we work, in four parts: a name, a
18	statement, a rationale, and implications. Terms the principles use —
19	rendering, anchor, definition chain, and the rest — are defined in the
20	[glossary](glossary.md); the processes and tools the implications name
21	are defined in this basis's sibling documents.
22	
23	- The **statement** is the rule. It carries the only normative keywords
24	  (MUST, SHOULD, MAY — interpreted per BCP 14 when, and only when, they
25	  appear in capitals) and is testable: shown a piece of work, you can
26	  answer yes or no. A statement carrying more than one obligation
27	  presents one obligation per bullet.
28	- The **rationale** says why the rule earns its place: the failure it
29	  prevents, shown as a generic example; well-known external references
30	  may support it. Rationales stay prose.
31	- The **implications** are the price tag: one implication per bullet,
32	  the concrete change each named actor absorbs to honor the rule. They
33	  add no obligations — every implication must be derivable from the
34	  statement, or it is a misfiled rule.
35	
36	A principle is good when its statement is testable (TOGAF, The Open
37	Group Architecture Framework: understandable, complete, consistent), it
38	rejects something we would otherwise do (Jared Spool, "Creating Great
39	Design Principles"), it directs without prescribing method (Richard
40	Rumelt, *Good Strategy Bad Strategy*), it is not a claim every shop
41	would make (Patrick Lencioni, "Make Your Values Mean Something",
42	Harvard Business Review, 2002), and it implies at least one practice
43	and one check. The fitness screen at the end of this document applies these tests
44	to the principles above it.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Define what good looks like up front (`define-good-up-front`)
49	
50	**Statement.**
51	
52	- Every activity MUST operate from a stated definition of what good
53	  looks like.
54	- That definition MUST drive both the performance of the activity and
55	  its check.
56	- The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different
57	  accountability.
58	- The maker of an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check,
59	  and record that it did.
60	
61	**Rationale.** A definition applied only at the check puts the full weight
62	of quality after implementation, where rework is most frequent and most
63	expensive. A definition applied only up front invites gaming and closes
64	off outside perspective. Two roles reading one definition give both
65	prevention and challenge. (Deming: cease dependence on inspection; build
66	quality in — and still inspect.)
67	
68	**Implications.**
69	
70	- Authors of new activities ship the definition with the activity, or
71	  the activity does not enter the system.
72	- A check that cannot cite the definition clause it projects has no
73	  standing; anyone may remove it without a new decision.
74	- Reviewers compare work to the written definition; their own taste is
75	  not the standard.
76	- The same role never both performs and checks an activity — process
77	  definitions name both roles, so this is checkable mechanically.
78	- A failed spot check sends the maintainer to the definition or the
79	  check, not only to the artifact.
80	- Whoever proposes a new activity writes the proposal as a draft
81	  instance of the activity's type, so the type's derived checks run on
82	  the proposal before any reviewer reads it.
83	
84	## Govern the generating context (`governed-context`)
85	
86	**Statement.**
87	
88	- Everything loaded into an agent's generating context — prompts,
89	  skills, memories, primers — MUST trace to an approved definition or a
90	  governed record.
91	- An unsanctioned context channel MUST NOT be created or retained.
92	
93	**Rationale.** What an agent reads determines what it produces, so an
94	ungoverned context input is an ungoverned generator. The failure
95	mode this prevents: notes accumulate in channels no process governs, and
96	work comes to depend on content no one has ever reviewed.
97	
98	**Implications.**
99	
100	- Maintainers version every context input.
101	- Maintainers promote changes through a gated step.
102	- Maintainers can audit which definition version was in force when an
103	  artifact was produced.
104	- Whoever operates a context channel closes it when it lacks a defined
105	  process and a consumer.
106	- Tool owners ship each tool's skill with the tool, in lockstep.
107	
108	## Every activity belongs to a process (`no-orphan-activities`)
109	
110	**Statement.**
111	
112	- Every activity in the system MUST be part of a defined process with
113	  stated expected outcomes, expected outputs, and possible resulting
114	  actions.
115	- Every long-running loop MUST declare its exit — a reached-state
116	  success exit, a round or budget cap, or both.
117	
118	**Rationale.** An activity outside a process has no consumer for its
119	output, so the output piles up unread or is thrown away. Both
120	failure modes follow: feedback stops flowing when nothing consumes it, and
121	the signal migrates into ungoverned channels instead. Any runtime can follow a process defined at this
122	level — the requirement is a definition, not a workflow engine.
123	
124	**Implications.**
125	
126	- Reviewers treat an activity with no process as a defect, not a
127	  convenience.
128	- Authors have no cost excuse: a process definition is a header plus a
129	  data section and a steps section.
130	- Reviewers fail any loop without a declared exit.
131	
132	## Use defined terms (`use-defined-terms`)
133	
134	**Statement.**
135	
136	- Important terms MUST be defined in the system, in the glossary or as
137	  a schema element.
138	- A term is important when a reader must know it to perform or check
139	  the work.
140	- When more than one term could carry a statement, the writer MUST use
141	  a defined term if one is available.
142	
143	**Rationale.** The defined-term list — glossary entries plus schema
144	element names — restricts the available language, and a restricted
145	language aids clarity and reduces drift. The failure is cheap to reach:
146	two words for one thing appear within days of each other, and every
147	reader of both must learn they are the same.
148	(Controlled-vocabulary practice: ASD-STE100, ISO 704.)
149	
150	**Implications.**
151	
152	- Writers check the glossary and the schemas before coining a term; an
153	  undefined important term is a defect the author repairs by defining
154	  it or replacing it with a defined one.
155	- Schema authors are vocabulary authors: naming a field adds a term to
156	  the restricted language.
157	- Reviewers flag near-synonym pairs as drift; the losing term is
158	  removed everywhere, not deprecated in place.
159	- When in doubt whether a term is important, the writer defines it.
160	
161	## Use external standards first (`external-standards-first`)
162	
163	**Statement.**
164	
165	- A definition MUST adopt an established external form where one fits.
166	- Bespoke structure MUST be justified by a recorded gap in the form it
167	  rejects.
168	
169	**Rationale.** Established forms carry decades of failure-tested
170	decisions no fresh invention can match, and readers arrive already
171	knowing them. The failure a bespoke form invites: a home-grown format
172	half-copies the standard it ignored, every reader must learn it from
173	scratch, and it silently diverges from the tooling and expectations the
174	standard would have supplied for free. In practice every element of a
175	definition system has an established form, and the only bespokeness that
176	survives review is the composition of adopted parts.
177	
178	**Implications.**
179	
180	- Authors search prior art before drafting and name every adopted form
181	  in the definition's Sources section.
182	- Reviewers ask "what standard is this from" and treat unjustified
183	  invention as a defect.
184	
185	## Single source of truth (`single-source-of-truth`)
186	
187	**Statement.**
188	
189	- Every fact, rule, or definition MUST have exactly one authoritative
190	  home.
191	- Every other appearance MUST be a reference or a generated rendering.
192	
193	**Rationale.** Copies drift and each drifting copy trains a different
194	behavior. Copies of schemas drift from their source, and
195	pinned example links stop conforming as the source moves on.
196	
197	**Implications.**
198	
199	- Writers link or `$ref` instead of restating.
200	- Only the compiler touches renderings; a hand edit to a rendering is
201	  reverted, not merged.
202	- Reviewers treat a second authoritative statement of one rule as a
203	  defect and remove the losing copy everywhere.
204	
205	## Feedback loops have consumers (`feedback-loops-with-consumers`)
206	
207	**Statement.**
208	
209	- Every feedback channel MUST name its consumer and the resulting
210	  action.
211	- The effectiveness of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be measured.
212	- The definitions of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be updated from
213	  what is measured.
214	
215	**Rationale.** A channel without a consumer dies silently and takes its
216	signal with it: when nothing consumes a channel, senders stop sending
217	and the signal moves into ungoverned channels. Judged checks decay the same way when no one
218	grades the judge.
219	
220	**Implications.**
221	
222	- Whoever opens a channel names its consumer and resulting action at
223	  creation, or the channel is closed.
224	- Owners of judged checks grade a sample of verdicts on a standing
225	  calibration schedule.
226	- Definition owners treat measured ineffectiveness as an obligation to
227	  update the definition, not as background noise.
228	
229	## Delivery is verified in the running system (`delivery-verified`)
230	
231	**Statement.**
232	
233	- Work MUST be counted done only when its effect is demonstrated in
234	  the running system.
235	- Artifacts existing, checks passing, or reviews approving MUST NOT
236	  count as done on their own.

238	**Rationale.** The gap between green artifacts and working systems is
239	where the worst defects live: builds publish without the built thing
240	ever running, and checks stay green while decided behavior goes
241	unrealized.
242	
243	**Implications.**
244	
245	- Definition authors name the runtime demonstration in every
246	  Definition of Done.
247	- Reviewers reject completion claims that cite only artifacts.
248	- Whoever closes work cites the demonstration evidence in the close
249	  reason — the reconcile process enforces this shape.
250	
251	## Load the least context (`least-context`)
252	
253	**Statement.**
254	
255	- An activity MUST load the minimum context necessary to accomplish
256	  its task.
257	- The activity's process MUST name what loads into context and the
258	  source each input comes from.
259	- Context from an unapproved source MUST NOT be loaded.
260	
261	**Rationale.** Extraneous context costs twice: tokens spent carrying it,
262	and drift when the agent follows something it was never meant to read.
263	The failure mode this prevents: unreviewed notes loading into every
264	session regardless of task, and unscoped conversations no one can
265	associate with specific work. (Least privilege, applied to context.)
266	
267	**Implications.**
268	
269	- Process authors declare a step's context inputs the way they declare
270	  data inputs — the declared list is the load list.
271	- Whoever runs a session loads a conversation's anchor and its
272	  definition chain, nothing ambient.
273	- Maintainers keep historical stores — archives, transcripts — out of
274	  ambient context; reading one is a deliberate, declared act.
275	- Reviewers treat an undeclared context load as a defect.

# Fitness set: principle-set

These scenarios are evaluated by the `cold-reviewer` role, never executed
— no step definitions exist or will exist. The judge's model and prompt
version are recorded with each round verdict. The mapping table at the
end compiles each Then into the judge-rubric assertion the reviewer
scores. The scenarios project the set's own opening tests (the
self-definition the typedef requires) and the
[principle-set guideline](../guidelines/principle-set.md)'s rules into a
judge's rubric.

## Scenarios

Scenario 1: good is defined before any instance, and only the four parts appear
  Given the principle set read top to bottom
  When the reader reaches the first principle
  Then the opening has already defined the four parts and the tests a
  good principle passes
  And each principle carries exactly a slugged name, a statement, a
  rationale, and implications — nothing else
  And every cross-reference to a principle uses its slug, never a number

Scenario 2: the statement decides alone, clause by clause
  Given any principle's statement and one concrete piece of work
  When a reviewer holds the work against the statement alone
  Then the reviewer can answer yes or no without reading the rationale
  or the implications
  And a statement carrying more than one obligation presents each
  obligation as its own bullet, with conditional logic kept inside its
  bullet
  And every term the decision turns on is defined in the statement, the
  set's opening, or the glossary

Scenario 3: the rationale shows a generic failure
  Given any principle's rationale
  When its evidence is checked
  Then it names the failure the rule prevents with a generic example,
  references no operational history of the product — artifacts, issues,
  incidents, decision records, or counts — and cites, at most, well-known
  external references as support

Scenario 4: implications are a derivable price tag
  Given each implication
  When it is traced back to its principle's statement
  Then it names the actor who absorbs the change, follows from a
  statement clause, and adds no obligation the statement does not carry
  And each implication stands as its own bullet

Scenario 5: the screen covers the set
  Given the set's fitness screen table
  When it is compared against the principles and the opening's tests
  Then every principle has a column, every test has a row, and every
  claimed pass is one the judge can reproduce

Scenario 6: each principle rejects something
  Given any principle
  When asked what work it rules out
  Then it rejects work this shop would otherwise do, and the opposite
  rule is one an honest shop could adopt

## Compile mapping (each Then/And → one judge-rubric assertion)

| Scenario Then | Judge-rubric assertion (established format, tool chosen later) |
|---|---|
| 1 (Then) — good defined first | "Does a self-definition (the four parts and the tests) appear before the first principle? Yes/no; cite the heading." |
| 1 (And) — four parts only | "For each principle, list any content outside name, statement, rationale, implications. Empty list = pass." |
| 1 (And) — slug citations | "List every cross-reference to a principle made by number or position instead of slug. Empty list = pass." |
| 2 — statement decides alone, clause by clause | "For each statement: could you accept or reject a concrete piece of work from the statement alone? Is each obligation its own bullet where more than one is carried? Name any term the decision turns on that is undefined in the statement, the opening, or the glossary. A fused multi-obligation sentence or an undefined decision term = fail, cite it." |
| 3 — rationale shows a generic failure | "For each rationale, quote the generic failure example. Any reference to the product's operational history — an artifact, issue, incident, decision record, or count — = fail, cite it. Any external reference cited must be a well-known published source, standard, or named law." |
| 4 — implications derivable, actor-named | "For each implication, name the actor and the statement clause it follows from. Any implication with no actor or no clause, or two implications fused in one bullet = fail, cite it." |
| 5 — screen covers the set | "Is there a column per principle and a row per test? Is any claimed pass one you cannot reproduce? Cite mismatches; none = pass." |
| 6 — rejects something | "For each principle, state the work it rejects and the opposite rule. If it rejects nothing we would otherwise do, or no honest shop could adopt the opposite, = fail." |

findings:
- criterion: Scenario 2 (And — one obligation per bullet)

  quoted: "The maker of an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check, and record that it did."

The bullet carries two obligations joined by "and", which the opening's own rule ("A statement carrying more than one obligation presents one obligation per bullet") and the criterion both forbid. Note the opening's rule is the set's own fourth-part test, so the fitness-screen "Statement testable" cell for this column is judged on a bullet that breaks the set's stated form.
  decided: confident
- criterion: Scenario 2 (And — decision terms defined)
  section: define-good-up-front / statement, fourth bullet
  in_amendment: yes
  quoted: "The maker of an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check, and record that it did."
  change: Introduce or replace "maker" and "record". "maker" appears nowhere else in the set — the rest of the document says Authors, Writers, Whoever proposes/opens/closes — and the opening does not define it; I cannot read the glossary, so I cannot decide whether it is defined there. "record that it did" gives a reviewer no way to say where a record counts (a history entry? a line in the submission? anything?): the decision "did the maker record it" turns on a term the statement does not pin. Either use the set's existing actor vocabulary and name the record's home, or confirm both are glossary terms.
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: Scenario 5 (every claimed pass is one the judge can reproduce)
  section: Fitness screen / row "Helps you say no (Spool)", column define-good-up-front
  in_amendment: no (the cell is unchanged; the amendment changes what it means)
  quoted: "yes: rejects definition-less checks and self-checked work"
  change: Restate the cell so it does not read against the new statement. Before v8 "rejects self-checked work" was reproducible: the third bullet puts the check with a different role. After v8 the fourth bullet requires the maker to evaluate its own output before submission — a reader holding the cell against the statement now sees the principle both rejecting and mandating a form of self-checking, and has to guess that "self-checked" means "checked by the maker alone". The history entry's gloss ("rejects unevaluated submission as it rejects self-checked work") does the reconciling, but history is not the screen. Something like "rejects checks held by the maker alone, and submission without the maker's own evaluation" makes the pass reproducible from the table.
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: uncovered
  section: define-good-up-front / statement, fourth bullet
  in_amendment: yes
  quoted: "- The maker of an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check,\n  and record that it did."
  change: Re-wrap to the document's line width. Every other bullet in the set wraps at roughly 72 columns; this one runs the first line long and breaks only before "and record". It is the one visibly unedited-looking line in the document and is where a cold reader's eye stops first. Cosmetic; no criterion names it.
  decided: confident

Sections with no findings: Scenario 1 (the four parts and the tests precede the first principle; every principle carries exactly name, statement, rationale, implications; no cross-reference by number) — clean. Scenario 3 (every rationale, including define-good-up-front's unchanged one, names a generic failure and cites only Deming, ASD-STE100/ISO 704, least privilege; no artifact, issue, incident, decision record, or count) — clean; the unchanged rationale's first sentence, "A definition applied only at the check puts the full weight of quality after implementation", is in fact the failure the fourth bullet prevents, so the amendment did not orphan it. Scenario 4 (implications) — clean; no implication was added for the fourth bullet, and the criterion does not require one; the sixth implication ("Whoever proposes a new activity writes the proposal as a draft instance ... before any reviewer reads it") already follows from it. Scenario 6 — clean; the fourth bullet rejects submitting unevaluated work, and "let the check find it" is a rule an honest shop could adopt. All other principles — no findings.
